source: Netball Skills and Conditioning Manual, Level 1, 3rd version, Niel du Plessis and Erin Burger, Passing section, page 81, heading '1 HAND HIGH PASS' at manual line 2670. Three numbered steps at 2672, 2673 and 2674, and four warnings at 2676. THE LIBRARY'S FIRST ONE-HANDED PASS. ITS DEFINING CUE IS NOT GRADED: step 1, 'Pull the ball up as high as arm can go', is a HEIGHT, and the library has no units-correct height measure. It is recorded as a gap rather than given a proxy, ruled by the orchestrator on 2026-09-04. The numeric bands are NOT the manual's. They are PROVISIONAL and a coach must set them. Refer to docs/ONE_HAND_HIGH_INSTRUMENT_AUDIT.md.
heightGapNote: STEP 1 IS THE DRILL'S DEFINING CUE AND IT HAS NO CHECKPOINT. “Pull the ball up as high as arm can go” is a height in centimetres. Nothing in segment_measures.MEASURE_UNITS reads a height except footHeightGapCm, and no band field holds centimetres. The available proxy is rightShoulderElevationDegrees, which netball_overhead_pass ships on for the same cue, AND IT IS WEAKEST EXACTLY HERE: docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md records that its leak into arm fold and hand placement GROWS with height, 8.2 degrees of spread with the ball at 184.4 cm against 3.7 near the crown line at 174.1. This drill puts the ball at 199.95 cm, above both. So the substitute would be least pure precisely where this drill lives. THE GAP HAS AN OWNER AND A DATE: a units-correct height measure, ball centre or wrist height in centimetres at the graded phase, declared in MEASURE_UNITS with a centimetre band field, is the movement lane's next engine unit after its current pack, ruled 2026-09-04. When it exists, step 1 gets its checkpoint here.
reachNote:
WHAT 'AS HIGH AS ARM CAN GO' ACTUALLY REACHES, measured on THIS drill at its final authoring, because the cue is not graded and a reader deserves the number anyway. Ball centre peaks at 199.95 cm at frame 34; the right wrist peaks at 185.27 cm at frame 31. On this drill at frame 0, from the floor: chest 125.99 cm, right shoulder 131.32, crown 163.44, and shoulder plus upper arm plus forearm puts a straight arm's wrist at 184.00. THE WRIST GOES 1.27 cm ABOVE THAT because the shoulder itself rises when the arm goes overhead, so the frame-0 construction is a LOWER BOUND and not a ceiling.

EVERY FIGURE ABOVE IS FROM THIS DRILL AND NOT FROM ITS NEIGHBOUR. The audit that preceded this file quoted the same landmarks from netball_overhead_pass, where the chest is 126.32 and the straight-arm wrist is 185.55. The frame-0 pose is not identical between drills, so those are that drill's numbers and not this one's. Mixing them is the fault class docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md records, and the audit is corrected rather than quietly left.

A FINGERTIP HEIGHT IS NOT A REACH FIGURE AND IS NOT QUOTED HERE. The audit offered one. Measured, the wrist-to-fingertip distance at frame 0 is 6.83 cm on this drill and 13.24 on netball_overhead_pass, because it is read along whatever direction the fingers happen to point and the grip pose differs. A construction whose input moves 6.4 cm between two drills of the same athlete is not a skeletal limit. The wrist figure is, because shoulder plus two segment lengths does not depend on the hand.

THE COMPARISON WITH netball_overhead_pass IS LIKE FOR LIKE: both are BALL CENTRE peaks, 199.95 here against 184.41 there, so this drill carries the ball 15.54 cm higher. That is the difference the manual's two different sentences describe, 'as high as arm can go' against 'into the air above your head'. NONE OF THESE NUMBERS IS GRADED.
freeArmNote: THE LEFT ARM DOES NOT MOVE AT ALL, AND THAT IS A FIRST FOR THIS LIBRARY. leftElbowFlexionDegrees reads 34.53 on every one of the 96 frames, a span of 0.00 degrees, and the left shoulder moves 4.38 degrees, which is under the 5 degree threshold. SO NO CHECKPOINT ON THE FREE ARM IS POSSIBLE HERE: one would be exactly the insensitive checkpoint this library has twice authored and withdrawn. The two existing one-handed drills are NOT like this. netball_one_hand_snatch_to_other_hand moves its left elbow 32.61 degrees and netball_hooks_outside_hand moves its 30.55, because both bring the second hand ONTO the ball at a secondHand phase. This drill has no second hand, so nothing ever asks the free arm for anything. The manual is silent about the free arm in this block, so nothing is lost against the source; it is recorded because a reader comparing the three one-handed drills would otherwise expect a free-arm checkpoint and find none.
sideNote:
THE FOUR ARM MEASURES HERE ARE ALL ON THE RIGHT, AND EVERY OTHER PASS IN THIS LIBRARY GRADES THE LEFT ARM. The right is the working arm, following netball_hooks_outside_hand and netball_one_hand_snatch_to_other_hand, the library's only other one-handed drills. Copying the nearest pass's left-side rows would have graded the arm that never moves, and the audit wrote that trap down before this file was authored.

THE FIFTH CHECKPOINT IS leftKneeFlexionDegrees AND IT IS ON THE LEFT. An earlier version of this note said every graded measure here is on the right, which is wrong by that one. It is the library's common stance reading, graded on the left on every drill including this one, and it is not an arm measure at all. So the accurate statement is four arm measures on the right plus one left-knee reading, and not five right-hand measures.

checkpoints.cue: Start with the ball at your chest.
checkpoints.why: NOT A QUOTE. The manual gives this block no opening line, unlike the overhead pass which opens with a catch. The starting pose is carried from the other three passes so the family begins the same way, and this checkpoint says the arm is folded with the ball at her chest before anything is asked of it. A straight arm is ZERO flexion by segment_measures' convention, so a high number is a folded arm. BAND PROVISIONAL, taken from netball_chest_pass's ready.

NOT A QUOTE. The manual gives this block no stance cue at all. A balanced base before the throw, graded as every drill in the library grades it. GRADED AS A READING AND CLAIMING NO PROOF: refer to kneeProofNote. BAND PROVISIONAL.

checkpoints.cue: Arm straight at the top, not bent.
checkpoints.why: PART of manual 2672, step 1: 'Pull the ball up as high as arm can go'. READ THIS CHECKPOINT NARROWLY. It grades whether the arm is STRAIGHT, and it does NOT grade how high the ball is. An arm extended straight ahead reads the same as an arm extended straight up, so this cannot stand in for the height and it is not offered as one; the height is recorded as a gap in heightGapNote. What it does capture is real and is half the cue: 'as high as ARM can go' is a claim about the arm, and an arm bent at the top has not gone as far as it goes. BAND PROVISIONAL.

checkpoints.cue: Send it with the wrist and hand, do not push with the arm.
checkpoints.why: QUOTED, manual 2673, step 2: 'Give a small step, and with wrist and hands pass the ball'. ELIDED: 'Give a small step', which is a step LENGTH with no measure and is recorded as a gap. The elbow is what 'with wrist and hands' leaves for a checkpoint, the same reading the other three passes make, AND IT ALSO CARRIES THE WARNING at 2676, 'Don't push the ball with arm': a pass pushed by the arm is a pass thrown by extending the elbow through the release. BAND PROVISIONAL.

checkpoints.cue: The arm has come down and through as the ball leaves.
checkpoints.why: NOT A QUOTE, and it is here for a structural reason stated plainly. The elbow above moves only 4.07 degrees from the lift, which is UNDER the 5 degree threshold this project treats as the point where a difference means something. On THIS drill the arm is already straight at the top, so the elbow barely distinguishes a released pose from a lifted one even though it grades the manual's words correctly. The shoulder moves 31.12 degrees over the same interval and is what actually separates the two phases. WITHOUT THIS CHECKPOINT THE RELEASE PHASE WOULD NOT BE DISTINGUISHABLE and movement_definition.separation() would say so. THIS IS NOT THE HEIGHT PROXY WEARING ANOTHER HAT: it grades where the arm is at the moment the ball leaves, not how high the ball got, and step 1's height stays an ungraded gap. BAND PROVISIONAL.

noStepPhaseNote: THERE IS NO GRADED 'step' PHASE, THOUGH THE TECHNIQUE AND MOTION FILES BOTH HAVE A step KEY AT 0.55. The manual's step 2 opens with 'Give a small step' and its warning at 2676 is 'Don't give a too big step (shortening own 3ft)'. Both are step LENGTHS. Nothing in this engine measures a step length, so a graded step phase would have to be graded on something that is not the step, which is the substitution this pack exists to avoid. The step is authored in the motion file's rootAhead and is visible in the animation; it is simply not graded. This is the SECOND of the two cues in this block that the missing length measures cost, and it is counted in the ledger row alongside the height.
noInstrumentNote: THREE OF THE MANUAL'S CUES HAVE NO CHECKPOINT AND WILL NOT BE GIVEN A PROXY. Step 1's height, discussed in heightGapNote. Step 2's 'small step', discussed in noStepPhaseNote. And step 3 at 2674, 'Keep hand behind the ball and fingers up', together with its warning 'Don't move hand under ball': spikes/hand_orientation.py reports thumbToBallDegrees, thumbUpDegrees and fingerUpDegrees into every receipt and declares itself report-only. It is absent from MEASURE_UNITS, so no checkpoint can read it. A THIRD AND FOURTH DELETION WOULD BE A PATTERN: this library has already authored a checkpoint for a manual cue and removed it twice, on netball_chest_pass for being insensitive and on netball_overhead_pass for firing on a solver basin. So these cues are never authored rather than authored and withdrawn.
handReportNote: AND THE REPORT-ONLY HAND NUMBERS ARE READ ON A CORRUPT FRAME AT THIS DRILL'S RELEASE PHASE. hand_orientation.receipt_section reads round(atPhase * (frames - 1)), which for a release at 0.80 of 96 frames is frame 76 exactly. Measured on all three existing passes, at frame 76 and only at frame 76: the thumb tip sits 0.70 to 0.72 cm INSIDE the 11.00 cm ball, and the thumb swings 11.51, 15.81 and 19.83 degrees in that single frame on the bounce, chest and overhead passes, WHILE THE FINGERS HOLD THEIR ORIENTATION TO WITHIN 0.42 DEGREES. Frame 76 is the FIRST RELEASED frame and holdingTheBall already reads false there. Neither of the two carrying drills shows anything of the kind, so it belongs to the release transition and not to the grip. RECORDED, NOT FIXED, ruled 2026-09-04; the underlying pose is engine work. It matters to THIS drill more than to its siblings because step 3 and one of the four warnings are both about where the hand is, and this is the one drill where a single hand carries the whole cue.
kneeProofNote: THE KNEE CHECKPOINT IS A READING ON THIS BUILD AND CARRIES NO PROOF, which is different from every elbow and shoulder checkpoint in this file. The movement lane found that below the hips the solve can have no continuous dependence on the keys: planting rootAcross on every motion key in 0.01 arm-length steps gives knee gaps that oscillate and change sign, with joint jumps of 7 to 8 cm at the crossings. netball_bounce_pass reproduced that under the published lever after failing to reproduce it under a different one, and the lesson recorded there applies here unchanged: a sweep below the hips proves nothing and the lever is part of the experiment. The orchestrator ruled on 2026-09-02 that a knee checkpoint is authored if the manual cues it, graded as a reading, and not swept. THE MANUAL DOES NOT EVEN CUE IT HERE, so this checkpoint is the weakest in the file: it is the library's common stance reading rather than anything this block asks for. Refer to 'The lower body has no stable solution' in docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.
sweepNote:
THE THREE UPPER-BODY CHECKPOINTS ARE PROVEN BY PROGRESSIVE SWEEPS with their spacing stated, the method netball_overhead_pass established: at least three displacements, the measure must move progressively toward the edge, and the joint positions must move continuously AT THE CROSSING. 'Joint step' is the largest distance any single joint moves between one sweep point and the next, in centimetres, at the graded frame. Measured on the engine at eaecbb2's successor 46ed8a5 with this branch applied; the build named is the main commit, because the engine is what the figures depend on and a note cannot name the commit it lives in.

READY ELBOW, both ball keys swept ahead 0.55 / 0.70 / 0.85 / 1.00 in arm lengths, graded at frame 0: 136.35, 125.85, 111.40, 92.70, failing below 105. Monotone. Joint steps 12.11, 11.10, 10.21 — even, and no discontinuity.
LIFT ELBOW, lift carry up 1.42 / 1.30 / 1.18 / 1.06 / 0.94 in torso lengths, graded at frame 33: 60.56, 77.22, 97.51, 113.94, 128.05, failing above 85. Monotone. Joint steps 25.38, 8.15, 6.96, 15.19; the first is large because dropping the lift by 0.12 torso lengths moves the whole arm, and the crossing between 1.30 and 1.18 carries a joint step of 8.15, in line with the rest.
RELEASE ELBOW, release carry up, graded at frame 76, and THIS ONE NEEDS ITS BASINS DISCLOSED. Over the full range 1.24 to 0.60 the lever crosses four basins and the measure is not monotone — refer to basinNote. The PROOF is the sub-range 0.84 / 0.76 / 0.68, which is one continuous basin: 70.15, 79.06, 86.08, failing above 80, monotone, with joint steps of 3.92 and 3.72 cm AT AND ACROSS THE CROSSING. Three displacements, progressive, continuous where it matters.
RELEASE SHOULDER, the release carry's up over 0.92 / 0.84 / 0.76 / 0.68 in torso lengths, graded at frame 76: 99.66, 85.08, 77.84, 71.19, failing below 85. Monotone, with joint steps of 10.65, 3.92 and 3.72 cm, SO THE CROSSING ITSELF IS CONTINUOUS: the floor is passed between 0.84 and 0.76 on a 3.92 cm step. AN EARLIER VERSION PROVED THIS CHECKPOINT ON THE SPACING 1.24 / 1.05 / 0.86 / 0.67 / 0.48 AND STATED NO JOINT STEPS AT ALL. Those steps are 5.51, 19.95, 9.13 and 12.79, so that sweep crosses a solution boundary before it reaches the band and passes the floor on a 9.13 cm step. The measure was monotone either way; the proof was not, and the method this file claims to follow asks for continuity AT THE CROSSING. Found by the reviewer of 00c370a.

AND ONE CHECKPOINT COULD NOT BE PROVEN AND WAS DELETED. Refer to deletedCheckpointNote for the four levers that were tried on the follow-through shoulder and what each one did.
lobParentNote: THIS DRILL IS THE LOB'S MOST LITERAL PARENT, AND THE MANUAL SAYS SO THREE TIMES. The LOB PASS (BOMB) block at manual line 2720 reuses TWO of this block's three steps word for word: its step 2 (2725) is this block's step 1 (2672), 'Pull the ball up as high as arm can go', and its step 3 (2726) is this block's step 3 (2674), 'Keep hand behind the ball and fingers up'. Its own step 1 (2724) names its permitted parents: 'Use one of the different passing types (1 Hand high/wide or double hand)'. netball_overhead_pass shares NEITHER step verbatim; its step 1 at 2663 reads 'Pull the ball up into the air above your head', which is a different sentence and, measured, a different height: 184.41 cm against this drill's 199.95. So the library now holds two of the lob's three permitted parents, and the one whose wording the lob actually reuses. WHICH PARENT THE LOB RIDES IS STILL A COACH QUESTION and stays open in docs/LOB_AUTHORING_BRIEF.md; this file does not settle it, it only removes the reason the question could not be asked.
deletedCheckpointNote:
A FOLLOW-THROUGH CHECKPOINT WAS AUTHORED AND DELETED BEFORE THIS DRILL SHIPPED, and the evidence is kept because a deletion with no record is just an absence. It graded rightShoulderElevationDegrees at phase 1.00, reading 100.24 against a band of 60 to 115. IT COULD NOT BE PROVEN. Four levers were swept and none of them moved it out of its band:

  release carry up, 1.24 to 0.48 : 100.24, 97.70, 81.32, 79.65, 79.43 — span 20.81, never crosses, and a 20.57 cm pose jump inside it.
  release carry ahead, 0.96 to 1.36 : 100.24, 98.94, 97.72, 96.56, 95.46 — span 4.78, which is under the 5 degree threshold entirely.
  release carry across, -0.10 to 0.38 : 100.24, 100.55, 100.89, 101.26, 94.27 — span 6.99, never crosses.
  lift carry up, 1.42 to 0.94 : 100.24 at every point — SPAN 0.00. The lift key has no effect on this measure at all.

THE ONLY LEVER THAT CROSSED THE BAND WAS THE RELEASE PHASE, and it oscillated. The phase values were missing from an earlier version of this note, which made the walk unreproducible: release phase 0.80 and 0.88 both read 100.24, 0.93 reads 85.44, 0.96 reads 110.54 and 1.00 reads 128.44, with pose jumps of 19.97, 22.97 and 19.06 cm between the last four. That is a basin walk, not a measurement, and it is the exact fault that got netball_overhead_pass's pull-back checkpoint deleted on 2026-09-02.

WHY THIS DELETION IS NOT THE PATTERN noInstrumentNote WARNS ABOUT. The two earlier deletions removed checkpoints that had SHIPPED against MANUAL CUES. This one never shipped and grades nothing the manual says: this block describes no follow-through, and the checkpoint was the library's habit rather than the source's instruction. Nothing is lost against the manual by its absence. A COACH MAY STILL WANT A FOLLOW-THROUGH GRADED, and if she does, the engine cannot support one here until the release region is better determined — refer to basinNote.
basinNote:
THIS DRILL'S RELEASE REGION IS MARKEDLY LESS DETERMINED THAN ANY TWO-HANDED PASS'S, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN SUPPOSED. It is the reason the release carry was moved, the reason the follow-through checkpoint was deleted, and a finding in its own right.

THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON. The same lever, the release carry's up, swept over the same nine values from 1.24 to 0.60, on all four passes, reading the working arm's elbow at frame 76 and counting pose jumps over 5 cm:
  netball_one_hand_high_pass, hands=right : FOUR jumps, largest 21.87 cm, measure NOT monotone, largest single-step change 20.28 degrees.
  netball_overhead_pass, hands=both       : one jump, largest 7.50 cm, measure monotone throughout.
  netball_bounce_pass, hands=both         : two jumps, largest 7.01 cm.
  netball_chest_pass, hands=both          : one jump, largest 5.21 cm, largest single-step change 9.95 degrees.

THE ONE-HANDED DRILL HAS TWICE TO FOUR TIMES THE JUMPS AND ITS LARGEST IS THREE TIMES THE WORST OF THE OTHER THREE. A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT A DIAGNOSIS, offered so the question has somewhere to start: two hands on the ball constrain both arms and the trunk between them, and one hand leaves the free arm and the trunk with nothing asking anything of them, so the solve has more equally good answers to choose between. NOTHING HERE TESTS THAT. It is engine work and it belongs to the movement lane; refer to docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THIS FILE. The authored release carry sits inside a CONTINUOUS region, and its stability was checked rather than assumed: sweeping its ahead from 0.90 to 1.02 moves the release elbow 0.49 degrees in total, monotonically, and sweeping its up from 1.24 to 1.08 moves it 0.26. So the SHIPPED reading is stable. The basins are a problem for PROVING a checkpoint, not for the pose this drill actually holds.

THE CONTINUOUS REGION IS 0.80 TO 1.12, AND ABOVE 1.12 THE LEVER ALTERNATES BETWEEN TWO SOLUTIONS. An earlier version of this note said the basin ran unbroken from 0.80 to at least 1.34. THAT WAS FALSE, and it was false for the reason this pack exists to catch: it was read off a FOUR-POINT sweep at 0.92 / 1.06 / 1.20 / 1.34, every one of which happened to land on the same solution, so the sampling stepped over the alternation. Swept at 0.02 from 1.08 to 1.36 the picture is different: 1.14, 1.18, 1.28 and 1.30 read the OTHER solution, elbow 54.82, 54.49, 53.80, 53.72 with the shoulder near 100, while their neighbours read the shipped one, and the r_lowarm moves 21.67 to 22.19 cm between neighbours. Six jumps over 5 cm in that range. Found by the reviewer of 00c370a and reproduced here on the same engine.
